issues.legal_issue: Different allotment terms for rehabilitated stallholders and tender-selected licensees are consistent with equality when the groups are materially distinct and the difference rationally serves a public purpose.
material_facts: Stallholders had occupied stalls for decades, and the land they occupied was required for road widening.
The authority reserved shops for those stallholders to induce them to relocate and offered them a lower licence fee and relaxed zoning restrictions as part of their rehabilitation.

Other shops were allotted through tenders; the tender documents disclosed the reserved shops and the zoning restrictions, and the successful tenderers accepted those terms and offered licence fees above the reserved rates.
issues.conclusion: The rehabilitated stallholders formed a separate class, and the different licence fees and zoning terms were reasonable and rational; the differential treatment did not violate Article 14.
issues.legal_principle: Article 14 permits different treatment of distinct classes where the classification has a reasonable basis and serves a rational purpose. Rehabilitation of long-standing stallholders displaced for a public project, supported by relocation concessions, was a proper basis for different terms.

predicates.equality_challenge_to_differential_allot: A person challenging an authority’s allotment terms alleges unequal treatment in a proceeding reviewing the legality of that treatment.
predicates.displaced_occupants_needed_rehabilitatio: A group had occupied sites for a substantial period and had to leave because the sites were required for a public purpose.
predicates.concessions_induced_relocation_for_publi: The authority offered that group more favourable terms to induce relocation and facilitate the public purpose.
predicates.tender_allottees_accepted_disclosed_term: Other allottees obtained their interests through a tender process, knew the applicable terms, and accepted them.

issues.definition: When an equality challenge concerns different allotment terms, the terms are valid if long-standing occupants needed rehabilitation for a public purpose, concessions induced their relocation, and other allottees knowingly accepted different disclosed terms.

issues.legal_issue: Equality does not entitle a person to receive a benefit granted to another person, including a benefit that is unlawful or irregular.
material_facts: The tender allottees sought the lower fees and relaxed zoning restrictions given to the stallholders, or argued that the differences made their treatment discriminatory.
The tender allottees had accepted their own allotment terms, including the applicable fee and trade-zone restrictions.
The court held that a person may challenge an unlawful benefit given to another but cannot demand that the same unlawful benefit be extended to them.
issues.conclusion: The allottees could not claim the concessions given to the stallholders merely on grounds of equality.
issues.legal_principle: Article 14 guarantees equality as a positive right and does not require the State to repeat an illegality or irregularity. A claim under Article 14, including in proceedings under Article 226, must establish that a just and lawful entitlement was denied while being extended to others; Article 12 identifies the State authorities to which the equality guarantee applies.

predicates.equality_claim_seeks_extension_of_anothe: A claimant in an equality review proceeding asks the authority to extend to them a benefit granted to another group.
predicates.claimant_accepted_different_allotment_te: The claimant knowingly accepted allotment terms different from those granted to the other group.

issues.definition: A claimant who seeks another group’s benefit on equality grounds and accepted different allotment terms has no right to an unlawful or irregular benefit merely because it was granted to that group.

issues.legal_issue: An authority may enforce trade-zone restrictions that licensees accepted, and unequal non-enforcement against other licensees does not entitle a licensee to disregard those restrictions.
material_facts: The tender allottees were required to state the trades they proposed to conduct and undertook to comply with the published trade-zone plan.
Some allottees later conducted trades not permitted in their assigned zones and received notices concerning those breaches.
The court directed those who had deviated from their assigned zones to return to the permitted trades.
issues.conclusion: The zoning restrictions remained binding on the allottees who accepted them, and those who had deviated were required to resume the permitted trade in their assigned zones.
issues.legal_principle: The accepted terms of allotment required compliance with the trade-zone restrictions. Article 14 does not permit a licensee to avoid an accepted lawful condition merely because others have also breached it or have not been subjected to the same enforcement.

predicates.challenge_to_enforcement_of_license_cond: A licensee challenges enforcement of an allotment condition in a proceeding concerning the authority’s regulation of the licensed premises.
predicates.licensee_accepted_trade_zone_restriction: The licensee accepted a condition limiting the trade that could be conducted in the assigned zone.
predicates.licensee_operated_outside_assigned_zone: The licensee conducted a trade that was not permitted in the assigned zone.

issues.definition: A licensee who accepted a trade-zone restriction and operated outside the assigned zone must resume the permitted trade when enforcement of the condition is challenged.

issues.legal_issue: Where court orders delay payment of contractual arrears, the arrears may be made payable with interest and on equitable payment terms so that the court’s intervention does not prejudice the creditor.
material_facts: Interim orders had allowed some allottees to pay the reserved licence fee rather than the agreed fee while the proceedings were pending.
After the challenges failed, arrears of the agreed licence fees remained unpaid.

The court considered the duration of non-payment, the parties’ respective equities, and whether an allottee had deviated from the trade-zone restrictions; it ordered payment of arrears with simple interest, set different interest treatment according to the circumstances, and allowed payment by instalments.

The court also directed payment of the licence fee as revised under the licence terms, required deviating allottees to return to their assigned zones, provided for withdrawal of cancellation notices upon compliance, and denied the claimed damages.
issues.conclusion: The allottees were required to pay the contractual arrears with the interest and on the instalment terms set by the court; cancellation notices were to be treated as withdrawn upon compliance, and no damages were payable on account of cancellation.
issues.legal_principle: The maxim actus curiae neminem gravabit means that an act of the court shall prejudice no one. The court relied on Raj Kumar Dey v. Tarapada Dey, (1987) 4 SCC 398, in holding that the creditor could be awarded reasonable interest even though the interim orders had not expressly reserved that question.

predicates.proceeding_concerns_deferred_contractual: The proceeding concerns amounts due under an agreement whose payment has been disputed or deferred.
predicates.court_interim_orders_delayed_full_paymen: Interim court orders permitted payment of less than the full amount otherwise due while the proceeding was pending.
predicates.contractual_arrears_remain_unpaid: After the underlying challenge is resolved, amounts due under the agreement remain unpaid.

issues.definition: When interim court orders delay full payment of contractual amounts and arrears remain, the arrears are payable with reasonable interest on equitable terms.
